DBMS Code & Query Reference
Page 1

Theory-rich SQL and database reference for AI Tutor / RAG ingestion — organized by topic with
definitions, practical examples, query patterns, and reasoning.
Purpose: A structured DBMS curriculum reference covering relational concepts, SQL, normalization, transactions,
concurrency, indexing, modeling, and recovery. SQL syntax may vary slightly by database system.
DBMS Code & Query Reference
Page 2

The relational model represents data as tables of rows and columns. SQL is declarative: it states the required
result while the DBMS chooses an execution strategy.
Definition: A relation is a table; a primary key uniquely identifies rows and a foreign key represents a relationship to
another relation.

DDL
CREATE TABLE Student (
student_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
department VARCHAR(50),
cgpa DECIMAL(3,2)
);
Why It Works: CREATE TABLE defines the schema and integrity constraints.

DML
INSERT INTO Student (student_id, name, department, cgpa)

Filtering + projection
SELECT name, cgpa
FROM Student
WHERE cgpa >= 8.0
ORDER BY cgpa DESC;
Why It Works: WHERE filters rows, SELECT projects columns, and ORDER BY controls result ordering.
DBMS Code & Query Reference
Page 3

Constraints prevent invalid database states. Primary, candidate, unique, foreign-key, NOT NULL, and CHECK
constraints encode rules at the data layer.
Definition: Referential integrity requires a foreign-key value to correspond to an existing referenced key, unless NULL
is permitted.

Relationship constraint
CREATE TABLE Enrollment (
student_id INT,
course_id INT,
semester VARCHAR(20),
PRIMARY KEY (student_id, course_id, semester),
FOREIGN KEY (student_id) REFERENCES Student(student_id)
);
Why It Works: The composite key prevents duplicate enrollments for the same student/course/semester.

Domain validation
CREATE TABLE Course (
course_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
credits INT CHECK (credits BETWEEN 1 AND 6),
title VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL
);
Why It Works: CHECK restricts values directly in the database.
DBMS Code & Query Reference
Page 4

Joins combine related rows from multiple tables. INNER JOIN keeps matches; LEFT JOIN also preserves
unmatched rows from the left table.
Definition: A join combines tuples from relations according to a matching predicate.

Matching rows
SELECT s.name, e.course_id, e.semester
FROM Student s
JOIN Enrollment e
ON s.student_id = e.student_id;
Why It Works: Only students having matching enrollment rows appear.

Preserve left rows
SELECT s.name, e.course_id
FROM Student s
LEFT JOIN Enrollment e
ON s.student_id = e.student_id;
Why It Works: Every student remains; missing enrollment values become NULL.

Compare rows in one table
SELECT a.name, b.name
FROM Student a
JOIN Student b
ON a.department = b.department
AND a.student_id < b.student_id;
Why It Works: A table can be joined to itself to compare related rows.
DBMS Code & Query Reference
Page 5

Aggregate functions summarize groups using COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN, and MAX. GROUP BY creates groups
and HAVING filters groups after aggregation.
Definition: GROUP BY partitions input rows into groups on specified expressions.

Grouped aggregation
SELECT department, COUNT(*) AS student_count
FROM Student
GROUP BY department;
Why It Works: COUNT is evaluated separately for each department.

Filter groups
SELECT department, AVG(cgpa) AS avg_cgpa
FROM Student
GROUP BY department
HAVING AVG(cgpa) >= 8.0;
Why It Works: WHERE filters input rows; HAVING filters aggregated groups.
DBMS Code & Query Reference
Page 6

Subqueries nest one query inside another. EXISTS answers whether a related row exists, while UNION
combines compatible result sets.
Definition: A correlated subquery refers to values from the current outer row.

Compare with aggregate
SELECT name, cgpa
FROM Student
WHERE cgpa > (SELECT AVG(cgpa) FROM Student);
Why It Works: The inner query returns one average value used by the outer query.

Test relationship existence
SELECT s.name
FROM Student s

Normalization reduces redundancy and update anomalies. 1NF requires atomic values; 2NF removes partial
dependencies; 3NF addresses transitive dependencies; BCNF requires determinants to be superkeys.
Definition: X → Y means agreement on X implies agreement on Y.

2NF reasoning
Enrollment(student_id, course_id, student_name, grade)
student_id, course_id -> grade
student_id -> student_name
Why It Works: student_name depends on only part of the composite key, indicating a 2NF issue.

Normalize schema
Student(student_id, student_name)
Enrollment(student_id, course_id, grade)
Why It Works: Separating attributes by their determining keys reduces repeated data.
DBMS Code & Query Reference
Page 8

Transactions group operations into logical units. ACID describes atomicity, consistency, isolation, and
durability.
Definition: A transaction is a sequence of database operations treated as one logical unit.

UPDATE Account SET balance = balance - 500 WHERE account_id = 1;
UPDATE Account SET balance = balance + 500 WHERE account_id = 2;
Why It Works: COMMIT completes the transaction and makes its successful changes durable.
UPDATE Account SET balance = balance - 500 WHERE account_id = 1;

Why It Works: ROLLBACK discards uncommitted changes.
DBMS Code & Query Reference
Page 9

Concurrent transactions can produce dirty reads, non-repeatable reads, and phantom reads. Isolation levels
and locking coordinate concurrent work.
Definition: Two-phase locking has a growing phase for acquiring locks and a shrinking phase for releasing them.

Protect selected rows
SELECT balance
FROM Account
WHERE account_id = 1

Why It Works: Where supported, FOR UPDATE requests a lock suitable for a transaction that will modify the
selected row.

Why It Works: A savepoint allows later work to be undone without discarding earlier work.
DBMS Code & Query Reference
Page 10

Indexes add searchable access paths. They can speed reads but consume storage and add maintenance work
to writes.
Definition: An index is an auxiliary structure that helps locate table rows efficiently.

Lookup optimization
CREATE INDEX idx_student_department
ON Student(department);
Why It Works: Queries using department may benefit depending on data distribution and the optimizer.

Multi-column access
CREATE INDEX idx_student_dept_cgpa
ON Student(department, cgpa);
Why It Works: Column order matters; leading columns are especially important.

SELECT name FROM Student
WHERE department = 'CSE' AND cgpa >= 8.0;
Why It Works: EXPLAIN helps inspect scans, joins, and index choices.
DBMS Code & Query Reference
Page 11

Reusable abstraction
CREATE VIEW CSE_Students AS
SELECT student_id, name, cgpa
FROM Student
WHERE department = 'CSE';
Why It Works: The view encapsulates the filtering logic.

Multi-stage query
WITH HighScorers AS (
SELECT student_id, name, cgpa
FROM Student
WHERE cgpa >= 8.5
)
SELECT * FROM HighScorers
ORDER BY cgpa DESC;
Why It Works: The CTE gives an intermediate result a readable name.
DBMS Code & Query Reference
Page 12

Database programmability places reusable or automatic logic close to the data. Exact syntax varies across
PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, Oracle, and others.
Definition: A trigger automatically executes configured logic in response to database events such as INSERT,
UPDATE, or DELETE.

Encapsulate operations
-- Syntax varies by DBMS
CREATE PROCEDURE GetStudent(IN p_id INT)

Automatic auditing
-- Conceptual pattern
CREATE TRIGGER student_audit
AFTER UPDATE ON Student

INSERT INTO StudentAudit(student_id, changed_at)
VALUES (NEW.student_id, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP);
Why It Works: Triggers can automatically record changes; NEW/OLD syntax is DBMS-specific.
DBMS Code & Query Reference
Page 13

Entity-Relationship
modeling
identifies
entities,
attributes,
relationships,
and
cardinalities
before
implementation. Many-to-many relationships are normally resolved with an associative table.
Definition: Cardinality describes how many instances of one entity may participate in a relationship with another.

Student → Enrollment
Student(student_id, name)
Enrollment(enrollment_id, student_id, course_id)
Why It Works: One student can have many enrollments; each enrollment references one student.

Student ↔ Course
Student(student_id, name)
Course(course_id, title)
Enrollment(student_id, course_id, grade)
Why It Works: Enrollment resolves the many-to-many relationship.
DBMS Code & Query Reference
Page 14

Recovery mechanisms restore consistent database state after failures. Logging, checkpoints, and backups
work together to protect committed data and recover from operational mistakes.
Definition: Write-ahead logging records required recovery information before corresponding modified data pages are
considered safely written.
Why It Works: Checkpoints provide recovery points so less log history may need to be processed.

+ periodic incremental/differential backups
+ archived transaction logs
= recovery strategy
Why It Works: Backups protect against failures and destructive operations that ordinary transaction rollback
cannot undo.
